editor_note: The translation is faithful and would not mislead a learner. The job-status list, the pre-submission checks on run(), the runtime_jobs/runtime_sessions caveat and the security warnings all keep their meaning, and it uses "du" throughout. There are three small things a native editor would fix. In [4], "(über die IBM Quantum Platform API)" was moved after "Nutzer", so it now reads as applying to all three plans rather than only On-Prem. In [32], "jeweils nur einen … gleichzeitig" says the same thing twice. In [21], "muss Zugriff auf Qiskit Functions aktiviert haben" is a stiff calque of the English.

examples.suggested: Standardmäßig kann jeder Nutzer nur einen Funktions-Job gleichzeitig ausführen

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and a learner would not be misled. Entry [23] keeps the batch/session/backend mapping and the Open Plan caveat, and entry [3] keeps the parametrization condition. There are two small slips. QPU takes a different grammatical gender in different entries: masculine "den QPU" in [13] but feminine "der QPU" in [21]. In the tips list in [27], "Lerne, wie du lokal transpilierst, im Abschnitt [Transpile]" leaves the location phrase trailing after the subordinate clause, which reads awkwardly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The Open Plan session caveat, the requirement to supply parameter values, and the experimental-feature warning all survive, and the terms are used consistently (Circuit, Observable, Transpiler, Erwartungswert, du-register). What's left is small wording and grammar. The heading "Sampler Schnellstart" is missing its compound hyphen ("Sampler-Schnellstart"). "Die Schritte in diesem Thema" copies the English "topic" word for word, where a German writer would say "Artikel" or "Anleitung". The link title "zu clientseitigen Sampler und Estimator" doesn't decline the nouns properly for the plural.

examples.source: Sampler quickstart
examples.translation: Sampler Schnellstart
examples.suggested: Sampler-Schnellstart
examples.why: German compounds need a hyphen here. Without it the heading reads as two loose nouns.

examples.translation: Die Schritte in diesem Thema beschreiben, wie du den Sampler einrichtest
examples.suggested: Die Schritte in dieser Anleitung beschreiben, wie du den Sampler einrichtest

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. That includes the benchmark numbers, the ordering "vom niedrigsten zum höchsten", the population_size scaling example and the Gurobi comparison. The problems are small. Several English-style open compounds are missing their hyphens: "Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) Algorithmus", "Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) Problem", "beim Real Amplitudes Fall" and "die dynamische Portfolio-Optimierung (DPO) Function". Entry [16] also mixes singular and plural passive in one clause, and the step heading [31] "Ergebnisse abrufen" uses an infinitive where the other step headings use du-imperatives ("Lies", "Definiere", "Führe ... aus").

examples.source: uses the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) algorithm to solve a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem

editor_note: The German is faithful and reads naturally, with correct conventional terms (Hochverfügbarkeit (HA), Notfallwiederherstellung (Disaster Recovery), Single Point of Failure, Load Balancer). Entry [9], "keine spürbare Beeinträchtigung des Dienstes", keeps the English meaning exactly.

The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The Bell/GHZ explanations, the ⟨Z_0 Z_i⟩ decay and the resilience-level trade-off all carry over correctly, and the core terms are used consistently (circuit→Schaltkreis, observable→Observable, expectation value→Erwartungswert, entanglement→Verschränkung), with informal "du" throughout. What remains is minor. A few phrasings are stiff calques: "werden über ... Attribute ... aufgerufen" and "Zählungen" for counts in [49], "zeichne die Ergebnisse und bemerke" in [62], and "aufgrund des Vorhandenseins von Rauschen" in [64]. The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. editor_note: The meaning is faithful and nothing here would mislead a learner. In [22] the translation even fixes the source typo ("exported by our importer" becomes "von unserem Exporter"), which is correct. "Anweisung" is used for both "statement" (`gate`-Anweisung) and "instruction" (benutzerdefinierte Anweisung, CustomInstruction), so readers cannot tell the two apart in [29]/[30]. In [36], "benutzerdefiniertes Gate" stands for both Qiskit's auto-generated custom gate and the "user-defined custom gate", so the sentence seems to compare a thing with itself. [23] also drops "This discrepancy".

examples.source: Instead, Qiskit chooses a custom gate ... This can be less efficient that using one of the built-in standard gates, or a user-defined custom gate.
examples.translation: Stattdessen wählt Qiskit ein benutzerdefiniertes Gate ... weniger effizient ... als die Verwendung ... eines benutzerdefinierten Gates.

editor_note: The German keeps the meaning throughout, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Several passages still read like machine translation. In [3] the phrase "oder mit Qiskit Serverless bereitgestellt ausgeführt werden" merges "deployed" and "executed" into one garbled construction. In [18], "wird die Ausgabe pro-Shot-Messungen … sein" uses a stiff future tense and a malformed compound, and in [20] "Postselection auf inhärenten Eigenschaften" copies the English preposition. The term for quantum computing also changes within the file, appearing as "Quantum-Computing-Aufgaben" in [3], "Quantencomputing" in [21] and "Quantum Computing" in [21].

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The key technical passages are accurate: the bf-DCQO explanation (kontradiabatische Terme, Bias-Feld, nicht-variationell), the counts of 'bis zu zehnmal' and 'drei- bis viermal weniger verschränkende Gates', the AR definition and the benchmark caveats. Two small slips remain. In [45] the clause 'Da $(x_0, ..., x_4) \in \{-1, 1\}^5$ müssen wir' has no verb and needs 'gilt'. In [20], 'Einsammeln des Ergebnisses' is a stiff calque of 'collect the result'.

editor_note: The meaning matches the English throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The 50-qubit ceiling, the retirement date of 15 May 2024, the Open Plan caveat on sessions and the note that local testing mode has no built-in error mitigation all come through intact. The one defect is grammatical gender for "Backend", which switches within the file. It is masculine in [25] ("einen Qiskit-Aer-Backend") and [37] ("einen Aer-Backend") but neuter in [29] ("ein Fake Backend"). The conventional form is neuter (das Backend), so [25] and [37] should be aligned with it.

editor_note: The translation is faithful, natural and consistently uses informal "du" (for example "Erfahre, wie du dich … engagieren kannst"). There is one grammatical slip in entry [5]. "entscheidend für die Gestaltung seiner Zukunft" uses the masculine/neuter possessive, so it grammatically refers to "Qiskit-Ökosystem" and not to "Quantentechnologie", which the English "its future" means. It should read "ihrer Zukunft". This is a small misreference, not a misleading claim.

examples.source: contributions from the open-source Qiskit ecosystem projects and developers are crucial in shaping its future.
examples.translation: sind Beiträge aus den Open-Source-Projekten des Qiskit-Ökosystems und von Entwicklern entscheidend für die Gestaltung seiner Zukunft.
examples.suggested: sind Beiträge aus den Open-Source-Projekten des Qiskit-Ökosystems und von Entwicklern entscheidend für die Gestaltung ihrer Zukunft.
examples.why: 'its' refers to quantum technology ('die Quantentechnologie', feminine), so the possessive must be 'ihrer'. 'seiner' grammatically points to the Qiskit ecosystem instead.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The tricky parts are all correct: subsystem ordering for tensor/expand in [21]/[23], operand order for compose/front=True in [25]/[26], the global-phase caveat in [38] and the CP caveat in [41]. The only problem is the plural of "operator", which switches between the English "Operators" (headings [7], [13], [18], [34], [36] and prose [19], [32], [37]) and the German "Operatoren" ([21], [23], [37], [38]). In [37] both forms appear in the same sentence. Separately, the heading in [34] "Umwandlung zu Operators" is unidiomatic; German would say "Umwandlung in Operatoren".

examples.source: Operators implement an equality method that can be used to check if two operators are approximately equal.
examples.translation: Operators implementieren eine Gleichheitsmethode, mit der geprüft werden kann, ob zwei Operatoren näherungsweise gleich sind.
examples.suggested: Operatoren implementieren eine Gleichheitsmethode, mit der geprüft werden kann, ob zwei Operatoren näherungsweise gleich sind.
examples.why: The same concept uses the English plural and then the German plural within one sentence. When the text means the class, it should say `Operator`-Objekte; otherwise it should say Operatoren.

examples.source: Implicit conversion to Operators
examples.translation: Implizite Umwandlung zu Operators
examples.suggested: Implizite Umwandlung in Operatoren
examples.why: The verb takes "in" ("umwandeln in"), as in [7], so "zu" is wrong here. The English plural "Operators" also clashes with "Operatoren" used elsewhere in the file.

examples.source: Operators may be combined using several methods.
examples.translation: Operators können auf verschiedene Weisen miteinander kombiniert werden.
examples.suggested: Operatoren können auf verschiedene Weisen miteinander kombiniert werden.
examples.why: This is generic prose about operators, so it should use the German plural "Operatoren", as [21] and [23] do.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The benchmark claims keep their meaning, including the noise caveat at 90 and 100 qubits in [21] and the small vs. large instances comparison in [32], and the binary-to-spin mapping example in [51] still matches its setup. I found three stiff spots a native editor would change. In [25], "Einreichungen …, die … an die Bibliothek gemacht wurden" is a calque. In [10], the English "problem unitary" is turned into a noun, "die Problem-Unitären". In [48], "die Kosten- oder Energiegröße" is an awkward way to say "the cost or energy". Otherwise the terms are consistent (Circuit-Tiefe, Hamiltonoperator, Nachbearbeitung, Zufalls-Sampling) and the page uses "du" throughout.

examples.source: correspond to submissions made to the library using the Parity Twine Optimizer

examples.suggested: entsprechen Einreichungen, die mit dem Parity Twine Optimizer bei der Bibliothek eingereicht wurden
examples.why: 'Einreichungen … gemacht' is a calque of 'submissions made'. German would use 'einreichen'.

examples.translation: Die Kodierung der Problem-Unitären, exp(...)
examples.suggested: Die Kodierung des unitären Problemoperators exp(...)

examples.suggested: Der `objective_value` gibt die Kosten bzw. Energie des Optimierungsproblems an.
examples.why: 'Kosten- oder Energiegröße' is a stiff, invented compound. A plain rewording reads more naturally.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the caveat paragraph [24] and the AND strategy in [20], and the text consistently uses du. There are three small slips. In [24], the list after "als Ergänzung zu" has the wrong case: it should read "rauschbewusster Circuit-Kompilierung oder probabilistischer Fehlerauslöschung". In [26], "Fehlerminderungs- und Unterdrückungstechniken" is capitalized mid-compound and loses "error" on the second half. Also in [24], "near-term quantum hardware" becomes "Quantenhardware der nahen Zukunft", a calque that suggests future hardware, when the English means the current (NISQ) generation.

examples.suggested: als Ergänzung zu Techniken wie Messfehlerminderung, rauschbewusster Circuit-Kompilierung oder probabilistischer Fehlerauslöschung

examples.translation: andere verfügbare Fehlerminderungs- und Unterdrückungstechniken
examples.suggested: andere verfügbare Techniken zur Fehlerminderung und -unterdrückung
examples.why: The capitalized 'Unterdrückungstechniken' breaks the compound and loses 'Fehler' on the second half, which is not the usual German hyphenation.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the broadcasting rules, Examples 1 to 4 and the BitArray axis description, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A few things read stiff or calqued. [42] "Die folgende ist eine visuelle Übersicht" copies the English syntax word for word. [24]/[25] render "array pairs that broadcast" as "die Broadcasting unterstützen", which is awkward. [39] uses "an einen QPU" where German normally says "die QPU" (die Recheneinheit). The gender of observable also shifts: the singular is "das Observable" ([10], [29]), but the plural is "Observablen", which is the plural of "die Observable".

examples.suggested: Beispiele für Array-Paare, die sich broadcasten lassen:

examples.translation: zur Ausführung an einen QPU gesendet werden
examples.suggested: zur Ausführung an eine QPU gesendet werden

editor_note: Faithful and natural in all 20 entries, with no drift in the numbers or dates (the Nighthawk r2 line keeps "120 programmierbaren Qubits und 458 physischen Qubits"), and the terms are used consistently ("Revision", "Heavy-Hexagonal-Gitter", "Gate-Fidelity", "TLS-Mitigationsfunktion").

The meaning is faithful throughout. The deprecation timeline (early 2025, v1.3.0 to v2.0.0), the calibration-builder workflow and the use_fractional_gates requirement for both R_X and R_ZZ all carry over, and the text consistently uses informal "du". The one thing to fix is that the Qiskit concept "pulse schedule" is rendered as "Pulssequenz" in [5] and [9]. This is the same word used for "pulse sequence" in [10], so it blurs the Schedule/ScheduleBlock object that [5] then refers to as `ScheduleBlock`. Keeping "Schedule" ("Puls-Schedules") would keep the Qiskit object recognizable.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The benchmark numbers, the caveat about classical processing time in [19] and the definition of the accuracy metric A all match the English. A native editor would still fix a few things. German compounds are left unhyphenated ("Estimator Primitive", "Performance Management Function", "Qiskit Function-Arbeitslast", "Redacted Bank Fallstudie" next to "BlueQubit-Fallstudie"). [26] has the redundant "Größere Problemgrößen" and turns "encouraged" into the stronger "ausdrücklich empfohlen". editor_note: The translation is faithful, and nothing in it would mislead a learner. The support caveats in notes 4 to 9 all come through intact, including the parsing limits of qiskit-qasm3-import v0.6.0, nested control flow not being allowed on hardware, and input variables not being executable. There are a few small slips. In [24], "as of July 2025" becomes "ab Juli 2025", which means "from July 2025 onward"; [21] and [23] correctly say "Stand Juli 2025". In [18], "always" is dropped from "backend execution always requires" ISA compilation. The headings in [1]/[3] use the English-style compound "OpenQASM 3 Feature-Tabelle" where German would hyphenate it as "OpenQASM-3-Feature-Tabelle".

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The conditions, quantities and caveats all match the English, including the scale-1.0-vs-unmitigated point, the complementary-scale precision caveat and the empirical-estimation limits. The main slip is terminology inconsistency. "circuit" is "Schaltkreis" through entry [31] and then switches to "Circuit" from [33] on. "layer" is "Schichten" in the table but "Layer" in [57]-[65]. "unique layers" is "einzigartige" in [21] but "eindeutige" in [62]. "Observable" is "die Observable" in most places but "ein Observable" in [59]. Smaller defects are a few lexical and grammar ones: "unbiasiertes Error Mitigation" in [11] (wrong gender and a clash with "unverzerrten" in [15]), "high-fidelity qubits" given as "hochpräzise Qubits" in [57]/[63] (where "Präzision" already means target precision), the typo "Gerätcharakterisierungsprotokoll" in [15], and stiff calques in [14].

examples.suggested: Hardware-Mapping auf Qubits mit hoher Fidelity
examples.why: Fidelity is not precision. The file uses 'Präzision' for the user's target precision, so this blurs the two concepts. The same problem appears in [63].

examples.translation: das aktive Volumen des Circuits
examples.suggested: das aktive Volumen des Schaltkreises

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the V1-to-V2 primitives section and the pulse and transpiler sections at the end. I found no drift or invented claims, and the du register holds. The problems are small. In [44] QuantumCircuit is feminine ("eine `QuantumCircuit`", "diese `QuantumCircuit`"), but [179] and [180] make it masculine ("ein `QuantumCircuit`", "einen `QuantumCircuit`"). The headings [1]/[3] read "Qiskit v1.0 Feature-Änderungen", which is an English-style noun stack a German writer would hyphenate as one compound. examples.translation: Qiskit v1.0 Feature-Änderungen
examples.suggested: Feature-Änderungen in Qiskit v1.0 (or Qiskit-v1.0-Feature-Änderungen)

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The problem is the grammatical gender of `Target`: it is masculine in [22] ("den Target", used twice) but neuter everywhere else ("ein benutzerdefiniertes Target" in [30], [40], [45], [49], and "ein Target" in [31]). editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and the beta caveat, "without sacrificing performance" and the Sampler/Executor capability contrast all come across correctly. editor_note: In the QPU-versioning table [37], "Sample changes" is translated as "Beispieländerungen" ("example changes"). The English means a change of the physical device sample, i.e. swapping the chip, which is a trigger for a major version. The German reads like a header label, so a learner loses one of the major-version conditions. The same table also has "Genauigkeiten" for fidelities, while the rest of the file uses "Treue". It uses "Auslassen eines Gates" for a gate being taken out of service, and "Umsiedlung der QPU", which is odd wording. Elsewhere, "Single-/Two-Qubit" and "Ein-/Zwei-Qubit" are mixed, and a few calques read stiffly ([82] "als denselben Fehler … aufweisend gemeldet", [85] "Als alle 0 gemeldet").

examples.suggested: Austausch des Chips (Sample-Wechsel)
examples.why: 'Sample' here is the physical QPU chip. 'Beispieländerungen' means 'example changes', which drops a real major-version trigger and reads like a header.

examples.source: Manual calibrations to improve fidelities; Dropping a gate for some duration of time; Moving the QPU to a new location

examples.suggested: zur Verbesserung der Fidelities/Treue; vorübergehendes Deaktivieren eines Gates; Verlegung der QPU an einen neuen Standort
examples.why: 'Genauigkeiten' conflicts with 'Treue' used for fidelity everywhere else in the file. 'Auslassen' and 'Umsiedlung' are unidiomatic.

examples.translation: Single-Qubit-Cliffords und Two-Qubit-Gates
examples.suggested: Ein-Qubit-Cliffords und Zwei-Qubit-Gates

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The Bernstein-Vazirani configurations (i)-(iii), the 44 % vs 95.3 % Bell-state fidelities and the "lower is better" caveats all match the source, and the "du" register holds. Two terms are inconsistent within the file. "Hidden bitstring" appears as "versteckter Bitstring" in the table and in [25], but as "verborgener Bitstring" in [41] and [60]. "Workload" is feminine in [7] and [9] ("die Workload") but masculine in the [42] heading ("Den Orbit-Workload"). There is also a stiff passive calque in [25] ("Ein veranschaulichendes Beispiel wird unten bereitgestellt").

examples.source: Choose the hidden bitstring and construct the logical circuit.
examples.translation: Wähle den verborgenen Bitstring und erstelle den logischen Circuit.
examples.suggested: Wähle den versteckten Bitstring und erstelle den logischen Circuit.
examples.why: The table and [25] use 'versteckter Bitstring'. Pick one rendering and use it everywhere, including [60].

examples.source: Prepare the Orbit workload
examples.translation: Den Orbit-Workload vorbereiten
examples.suggested: Die Orbit-Workload vorbereiten
examples.why: [7] and [9] treat Workload as feminine ('der Workload' as dative/genitive of 'die Workload', 'eine bestimmte Workload'), but this heading makes it masculine.

examples.source: An illustrative example is provided below.
examples.translation: Ein veranschaulichendes Beispiel wird unten bereitgestellt.
examples.suggested: Unten findest du ein anschauliches Beispiel.
examples.why: This is a word-for-word copy of the English passive. A German technical writer would put it more directly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful across the whole algorithm description, the benchmarks and the licensing section: Teilraum, Hamiltonoperator, Screening, Konfigurationswiederherstellung and the 20-qubit licence cap are all rendered correctly, and the du register holds throughout. There are four naturalness slips. In [19], "senkt die Kosten … auf denselben Genauigkeitsgrad" is a calque that reads as "reduces costs to the accuracy level" instead of "lower cost at the same accuracy". In [11], "intractable" becomes "schnell unlösbar", which adds "schnell" and overstates "not practically computable" as "unsolvable". In [18], "Spärlichkeit" is unidiomatic for sparsity, and in [25], "In diesem Schritt kann ein zusätzlicher Screening-Schritt" repeats "Schritt" awkwardly.

examples.source: reduces the cost to solve a problem of a given size to the same degree of accuracy
examples.translation: senkt die Kosten zur Lösung eines Problems gegebener Größe auf denselben Genauigkeitsgrad
examples.suggested: senkt die Kosten, ein Problem gegebener Größe mit derselben Genauigkeit zu lösen
examples.why: 'auf' makes the Genauigkeitsgrad the level that costs drop to. The intended meaning is lower cost at the same accuracy.

examples.source: but this becomes intractable for larger systems
examples.translation: wird aber für größere Systeme schnell unlösbar
examples.suggested: ist aber für größere Systeme praktisch nicht mehr berechenbar
examples.why: 'intractable' means computationally infeasible, not unsolvable. 'schnell' also does not appear in the source.

examples.source: exploit this sparsity
examples.translation: nutzen diese Spärlichkeit
examples.suggested: nutzen diese Dünnbesetztheit
examples.why: 'Spärlichkeit' is not the usual German term for sparsity in numerics and quantum chemistry.

examples.source: An additional screening step can be performed at this point
examples.translation: In diesem Schritt kann ein zusätzlicher Screening-Schritt durchgeführt werden
examples.suggested: An dieser Stelle kann ein zusätzlicher Screening-Schritt durchgeführt werden
examples.why: 'Schritt' appears twice in a row, and 'at this point' does not mean 'in this step'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and uses du throughout. Core terms are consistent: Schaltkreis, Shot, Primitive-Job and Zustandsvorbereitungsfehler. There are three small problems. Entry [7] makes the claim stronger than the English: "imperfections … can introduce state-preparation errors" becomes "ist nicht perfekt und führt zu Zustandsvorbereitungsfehlern", which drops the "can". Entry [0] adds "von Quantenschaltkreisen", which the source doesn't say. Entry [19] uses the stiff coinage "Quanten-Näherungsoptimierungsalgorithmus" for QAOA.

examples.source: However, imperfections in the reset process can introduce state-preparation errors.
examples.translation: Der Reset-Prozess ist jedoch nicht perfekt und führt zu Zustandsvorbereitungsfehlern.
examples.suggested: Unvollkommenheiten im Reset-Prozess können jedoch zu Zustandsvorbereitungsfehlern führen.
examples.why: The English says the errors can occur. The German says the reset always causes them, which makes the claim stronger.

examples.source: Explanatory content about dynamic repetition rate execution
examples.translation: Erläuterungen zur dynamischen Wiederholungsrate bei der Ausführung von Quantenschaltkreisen
examples.suggested: Erläuterungen zur Ausführung mit dynamischer Wiederholungsrate
examples.why: Adds 'von Quantenschaltkreisen', which is not in the source, and turns the technical term 'dynamic repetition rate execution' into a looser paraphrase.

examples.source: Quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA)
examples.translation: Quanten-Näherungsoptimierungsalgorithmus (QAOA)
examples.suggested: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)
examples.why: This is a stiff coinage. German texts usually keep the English algorithm name or just write QAOA.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout: nothing would mislead a learner. The coupling-map, SWAP, layout/routing and ECR/CX passages all match the source. Three small things need fixing. In [16], the slash construction "der/das dem Transpiler übergeben wird" reads like a stopgap and should be rephrased. "instruction" is rendered as "Befehl"/"Befehlssatz" in [37]-[39] but as "Anweisung" in [40]. "topic" is calqued as "Thema" in [17] and [23] ("Dieses Thema zeigt …"), where a German writer would say "Diese Seite" or "Dieser Leitfaden".

examples.source: stored in the Backend or Target provided to the transpiler
examples.translation: im Backend oder Target gespeichert, der/das dem Transpiler übergeben wird
examples.suggested: im Backend- oder Target-Objekt gespeichert, das dem Transpiler übergeben wird
examples.why: The 'der/das' slash is an MT stopgap for gender ambiguity. No native technical writer would publish it.

examples.source: as long as you provide the instruction ... no further instruction/pulse gates
examples.translation: solange du die Anweisung bereitstellst ... keine weiteren Anweisungs-/Puls-Gates
examples.suggested: solange du den Befehl bereitstellst ... keine weiteren Befehls-/Puls-Gates
examples.why: Earlier entries render 'instruction' as 'Befehl'/'Befehlssatz'. Switching to 'Anweisung' here is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: This topic shows several examples of passing information to the transpiler.
examples.translation: Dieses Thema zeigt mehrere Beispiele für die Übergabe von Informationen an den Transpiler.
examples.suggested: Diese Seite zeigt mehrere Beispiele dafür, wie du dem Transpiler Informationen übergibst.
examples.why: 'Thema' as a calque of the doc-section sense of 'topic' is unidiomatic. Entry [12] already correctly uses 'Diese Seite'.

editor_note: The German is faithful and reads naturally. "retired" is rendered consistently as "stillgelegt", the CRN note keeps its instance/backend conditions intact ("Wird keine Instanz angegeben, sind alle Backends und Jobs aller Instanzen deines Kontos verfügbar"), and the text keeps the informal du form throughout.

The translation is faithful and would not mislead a learner. Conditions and quantities match the English, including the mask shape (2, 3, 4) and the caveat about overlapping execution spans, and the du register holds throughout. A native editor would still fix a few spots. The link text "runtime options" in [25] was left in English. The same entry switches PUB to the masculine ("für jeden PUB"), while the rest of the file uses the neuter ("jedes PUB"). "von den aus dem Primitive angegebenen Laufzeitoptionen" in [6] is a stiff calque, and so is "Das Folgende ist ein visueller Überblick" in [17].
